claim: Tauopathies feature progressive accumulation of tau amyloids.
source: Tauopathies feature progressive accumulation of tau amyloids.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about tauopathies.

claim: Pathology may begin when tau amyloids amplify from a protein template, or seed, whose structure is unknown.
source: Pathology may begin when these amplify from a protein template, or seed, whose structure is unknown.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the mechanism of pathology initiation.

claim: Recombinant seed-competent tau monomer (Ms) triggered intracellular tau aggregation.
source: Recombinant Ms triggered intracellular tau aggregation
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Recombinant seed-competent tau monomer (Ms) induced tau fibrillization in vitro.
source: Recombinant Ms triggered intracellular tau aggregation, induced tau fibrillization in vitro
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Recombinant seed-competent tau monomer (Ms) self-assembled.
source: Recombinant Ms triggered intracellular tau aggregation, induced tau fibrillization in vitro, and self-assembled.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ms from Alzheimer's disease seeded aggregation.
source: Ms from Alzheimer's disease also seeded aggregation
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ms from Alzheimer's disease self-assembled in vitro to form seed-competent multimers.
source: Ms from Alzheimer's disease also seeded aggregation and self-assembled in vitro to form seed-competent multimers.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Crosslinking with mass spectrometry was used to probe structural differences in Mi vs. Ms.
source: We used crosslinking with mass spectrometry to probe structural differences in Mi vs. Ms.
evidence: This describes the experimental method used in the study.

claim: Crosslinks informed models of local peptide structure within the repeat domain which suggest relative inaccessibility of residues that drive aggregation (VQIINK/VQIVYK) in Mi.
source: Crosslinks informed models of local peptide structure within the repeat domain which suggest relative inaccessibility of residues that drive aggregation (VQIINK/VQIVYK) in Mi
evidence: This claim is based on inference from crosslinking data and computational modeling.

claim: Crosslinks informed models of local peptide structure within the repeat domain which suggest exposure of residues that drive aggregation (VQIINK/VQIVYK) in Ms.
source: Crosslinks informed models of local peptide structure within the repeat domain which suggest relative inaccessibility of residues that drive aggregation (VQIINK/VQIVYK) in Mi, and exposure in Ms.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from crosslinking data and computational modeling.

claim: Limited proteolysis supported the idea of differential exposure of VQIINK/VQIVYK sequences in Mi vs. Ms.
source: Limited proteolysis supported this idea.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from limited proteolysis experiments.

claim: Tau monomer has been considered to be natively unstructured.
source: Although tau monomer has been considered to be natively unstructured
evidence: This refers to established scientific consensus about tau monomer structure.

claim: The findings belie the assumption that tau monomer is natively unstructured.
source: Although tau monomer has been considered to be natively unstructured, our findings belie this assumption
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Initiation of pathological aggregation could begin with conversion of tau monomer from an inert to a seed-competent form.
source: initiation of pathological aggregation could begin with conversion of tau monomer from an inert to a seed-competent form.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the experimental findings.

claim: Amyloid-forming proteins include tau, synuclein, and expanded polyglutamine proteins such as huntingtin.
source: Amyloid-forming proteins include tau, synuclein, and expanded polyglutamine proteins such as huntingtin, among many others.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about amyloid-forming proteins.

claim: It is unknown how or why intracellular proteins such as tau transition from a relatively inert form to one that efficiently self-assembles into ordered structures in vivo.
source: It is unknown how or why intracellular proteins such as tau transition from a relatively inert form to one that efficiently self-assembles into ordered structures in vivo.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current scientific knowledge.

claim: Under defined conditions and relatively high concentrations (typically micromolar), recombinant tau monomer will form amyloid fibrils in vitro.
source: Under defined conditions and relatively high concentrations (typically micromolar), recombinant tau monomer will form amyloid fibrils in vitro.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about tau aggregation in vitro.

claim: The basis of spontaneous assembly of tau in cells is unknown.
source: However the basis of spontaneous assembly in cells is unknown.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current scientific knowledge.

claim: It has been suggested that a critical seed for tau amyloid formation is a single molecule based on extrapolation from kinetic aggregation studies.
source: Based on extrapolation from kinetic aggregation studies, it has been suggested that a critical seed for tau and polyglutamine peptide amyloid formation is a single molecule (Chirita et al., 2005; Bhattacharyya et al., 2005; Kar et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: It has been suggested that a critical seed for polyglutamine peptide amyloid formation is a single molecule based on extrapolation from kinetic aggregation studies.
source: Based on extrapolation from kinetic aggregation studies, it has been suggested that a critical seed for tau and polyglutamine peptide amyloid formation is a single molecule (Chirita et al., 2005; Bhattacharyya et al., 2005; Kar et al., 2011)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: An earlier study has proposed a tau multimer as the critical seed.
source: while an earlier study (among others [Ramachandran and Udgaonkar, 2013]) has proposed a tau multimer (Friedhoff et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Tau forms amyloids that underlie neurodegeneration in tauopathies.
source: Tau forms amyloids that underlie neurodegeneration in a variety of neuropathological syndromes, collectively termed tauopathies (Lee et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Tauopathies include AD and frontotemporal dementias.
source: These include AD and frontotemporal dementias, among many others.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about tauopathies.

claim: Tau will propagate an aggregated state from the outside to the inside of a cell, between cells, across synapses, and within brain networks.
source: Multiple groups, including ours, have now observed that tau will propagate an aggregated state from the outside to the inside of a cell, between cells, across synapses, and within brain networks (Sanders et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Tau trimers are the minimal unit of spontaneous cellular uptake and intracellular amyloid formation.
source: In prior work, we used size exclusion chromatography (SEC) to define tau trimers as the minimal unit of spontaneous cellular uptake and intracellular amyloid formation, and proposed this as the smallest particle capable of propagating aggregates between cells (Mirbaha et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: Biosensor cells and primary neurons take up tau aggregates via macropinocytosis.
source: Biosensor cells and primary neurons alike take up tau aggregates via macropinocytosis (Holmes et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Tau aggregates serve as highly specific templates to trigger intracellular amyloid formation.
source: The aggregates subsequently serve as highly specific templates to trigger intracellular amyloid formation (Holmes et al., 2014; Sanders et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Preincubation of cationic lipids such as lipofectamine with tau seeds facilitates their direct transduction into a cell, bypassing the physiologic uptake mechanism.
source: We have also determined that preincubation of cationic lipids such as lipofectamine with tau seeds facilitates their direct transduction into a cell, bypassing the physiologic uptake mechanism (Holmes et al., 2014; Furman et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Lipofectamine-mediated delivery into biosensor cells allows direct quantitation of seed titer for both tau and α-synuclein.
source: Lipofectamine-mediated delivery into biosensor cells allows direct quantitation of seed titer for both tau and α-synuclein (Holmes et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Tau is intrinsically disordered upon isolation from bacteria or mammalian cells and is relatively inert in terms of spontaneous self-assembly.
source: Tau is intrinsically disordered upon isolation from bacteria or mammalian cells and is relatively inert in terms of spontaneous self-assembly.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about tau properties.

claim: Under various conditions, including exposure to polyanions such as heparin, tau will form aggregates via nucleated self-assembly.
source: However under various conditions, including exposure to polyanions such as heparin, tau will form aggregates via nucleated self-assembly (Goedert et al., 1996; Pérez et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: It is unknown how experimental conditions for tau aggregation relate to the initiation of aggregation in human brain.
source: It is unknown how these experimental conditions relate to the initiation of aggregation in human brain.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current scientific knowledge.

claim: Fibril-derived monomer (Ms) exhibited seeding activity in cells when delivered with lipofectamine.
source: Upon incubation with Lipofectamine, we were surprised to observe seeding by monomer and larger assemblies alike, whether FL WT or 2A. (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: Inert monomer (Mi) had no seeding activity in cells.
source: We termed the inert monomer 'Mi,' and the seed-competent monomer 'Ms.'
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental data showing differential seeding activity.

claim: Monomer fraction retained ~80% of seeding activity after passing through a 100 kDa cutoff filter.
source: While monomer fraction retained ~80% of seeding activity, only ~20% of dimer seeding activity remained, and ~1–2% of trimer seeding activity remained (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Only ~20% of dimer seeding activity remained after passing through a 100 kDa cutoff filter.
source: While monomer fraction retained ~80% of seeding activity, only ~20% of dimer seeding activity remained, and ~1–2% of trimer seeding activity remained (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Only ~1–2% of trimer seeding activity remained after passing through a 100 kDa cutoff filter.
source: While monomer fraction retained ~80% of seeding activity, only ~20% of dimer seeding activity remained, and ~1–2% of trimer seeding activity remained (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Mi had no intrinsic seeding activity in vitro.
source: Mi had no intrinsic seeding activity. However Ms induced amyloid formation, albeit more slowly than trimer or unfractionated fibrils (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Ms induced amyloid formation in vitro, albeit more slowly than trimer or unfractionated fibrils.
source: However Ms induced amyloid formation, albeit more slowly than trimer or unfractionated fibrils (Figure 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Ms had an EC50 of ~10 nM in the seeding assay.
source: Ms had an EC50 of ~10 nM (Figure 1G), which was very similar to dimer and trimer (Figure 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Dimer and trimer had similar seeding potencies to Ms.
source: Ms had an EC50 of ~10 nM (Figure 1G), which was very similar to dimer and trimer (Figure 1H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: CD spectroscopy revealed no obvious structural differences between Mi and Ms.
source: We tested for obvious structural differences between Mi and Ms using CD spectroscopy, which revealed none (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: FCS accurately estimated the units of small assemblies (≤10 mer), but not larger assemblies (>10 mer).
source: As we previously observed (Mirbaha et al., 2015), we accurately estimated the units of small assemblies (≤10 mer), but not larger assemblies (>10 mer) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and citation to prior work.

claim: 100% of events in Mi showed a diffusion time consistent with a tau monomer.
source: When we evaluated Mi and Ms, 100% of events in each case showed a diffusion time consistent with a tau monomer (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: 100% of events in Ms showed a diffusion time consistent with a tau monomer.
source: When we evaluated Mi and Ms, 100% of events in each case showed a diffusion time consistent with a tau monomer (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: No cross-correlation between red and green signal was observed in Mi, indicating no detectable multimeric assemblies.
source: Furthermore, we observed no cross-correlation between red and green signal, indicating that neither preparation had detectable multimeric assemblies (Figure 2C,D,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D,H.

claim: No cross-correlation between red and green signal was observed in Ms, indicating no detectable multimeric assemblies.
source: Furthermore, we observed no cross-correlation between red and green signal, indicating that neither preparation had detectable multimeric assemblies (Figure 2C,D,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D,H.

claim: Dimer, trimer, and ~10 mer showed longer diffusion times consistent with the predicted assembly sizes and significant cross-correlation values.
source: By contrast, when we evaluated larger species such as dimer, trimer, or ~10 mer, we observed longer diffusion times consistent with the predicted assembly sizes, and significant cross-correlation values (Figure 2E–H)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2E-H.

claim: SEC efficiently excludes larger seeds from the monomer fraction.
source: This confirmed that larger, seed-competent assemblies do not appreciably contaminate the monomer fraction during SEC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Ms retained virtually all of its seeding activity after heating to 95°C for 3 hr and re-isolation by SEC.
source: In the first instance, after heating we re-isolated Ms purely as monomer that retained virtually all of its seeding activity (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Trimer assembly broke down to smaller assemblies, predominantly monomer, after heating to 95°C for 3 hr, each of which retained seeding activity.
source: The trimer assembly (fraction B8) broke down to smaller assemblies, predominantly monomer, each of which retained seeding activity (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: ~20 mer was largely stable following heat treatment at 95°C for 3 hr and retained its seeding activity.
source: The ~20 mer (fraction A5) was largely stable following heat treatment, and retained its seeding activity (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Exposure of Ms, dimer, and trimer to temperatures ≥ 85°C for 18–24 hr eliminated seeding activity at roughly the same rate for each.
source: Lower temperatures only slightly reduced seeding activity, whereas exposure of Ms, dimer, and trimer to temperatures ≥ 85°C for 18–24 hr eliminated it at roughly the same rate for each (Figure 4D–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D-G.

claim: The seeding activities of ~10 mer and ~20 mer were relatively heat-resistant.
source: By contrast, the seeding activities of ~10 mer and ~20 mer were relatively heat-resistant (Figure 4D–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D-G.

claim: The barrier to conversion of Ms to an inert form was calculated to be ~78 kcal/mol.
source: Using the multimodal model, we calculated the barrier to conversion of Ms to an inert form to be ~78 kcal/mol.
evidence: This claim is based on analysis of heat denaturation data using a multimodal model.

claim: Mi showed no evidence of self-association over 24 hr at 500 nM.
source: Mi, dimer, and trimer showed no evidence of self-association in this timeframe (Figure 5A,C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Ms readily formed larger assemblies when incubated alone at 500 nM over 24 hr.
source: By contrast, when incubated alone, Ms readily formed larger assemblies (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Mi did not form larger assemblies when mixed with dimer or trimer over 24 hr.
source: When we incubated Mi with dimer or trimer, we saw no change in the assembly population over 24 hr (Figure 5E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E,F.

claim: Ms mixed with dimer or trimer formed larger assemblies with a concomitant reduction in dimer and trimer peaks.
source: By contrast, when we mixed Ms with dimer or trimer we observed a growth of larger assemblies with a concomitant reduction in dimer and trimer peaks (Figure 5G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5G,H.

claim: After 15 min of heparin exposure, low but significant amounts of seed-competent monomer were detected.
source: After 15 min of heparin exposure, we detected low but significant amounts of seed-competent monomer, and much fewer larger assemblies (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Recombinant monomer not treated with heparin had no seeding activity at any time point.
source: Recombinant monomer not treated with heparin had no seeding activity at any time point (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: At longer heparin treatment times (1 hr, 4 hr) monomer fractions as well as larger assemblies all had strong seeding activity.
source: At longer heparin treatment times (1 hr, 4 hr) monomer fractions as well as larger assemblies all had strong seeding activity (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Heparin-derived Ms was relatively resistant to heat denaturation at 95°C, albeit less so than fibril-derived Ms.
source: Ms derived from heparin exposure was relatively resistant to heat denaturation at 95°C, albeit less so than fibril-derived Ms (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Sonication of Mi and purification by SEC did not produce any seed-competent species.
source: We noted also that sonication of Mi and purification by SEC did not produce any seed-competent species, eliminating the possibility that small assemblies of sonication-induced fragments accounted for seeding activity of Ms (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Denaturation of recombinant tau with 8M urea prior to crosslinking produced no intramolecular cross-links.
source: Denaturation of recombinant tau with 8M urea prior to crosslinking produced no intramolecular cross-links (data not shown), indicating that crosslinks observed under native conditions represented local structure.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data (though not shown in the manuscript).

claim: Crosslinks observed under native conditions represented local structure.
source: Denaturation of recombinant tau with 8M urea prior to crosslinking produced no intramolecular cross-links (data not shown), indicating that crosslinks observed under native conditions represented local structure.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental observation that denatured tau showed no crosslinks.

claim: In Ms, crosslinking of K150 with K254, K267, K274 or K280 all located between RD 1 and 2 was consistently observed.
source: In Ms, we observed a consistent crosslinking of K150 with K254, K267, K274 or K280 all located between RD 1 and 2.
evidence: This claim is supported by XL-MS data.

claim: Crosslinks between K150 and K254, K267, K274 or K280 tracked exclusively with Ms, both fibril- or heparin-derived.
source: These crosslinks tracked exclusively with Ms, both fibril- or heparin-derived (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by XL-MS data shown in Figure 7B,C.

claim: Crosslinks between K150 and K254, K267, K274 or K280 were never observed in Mi.
source: We never observed these crosslinks in Mi.
evidence: This claim is supported by XL-MS data.

claim: The crosslink pattern between K150 and residues in RD1/2 persisted with seeding activity after heat denaturation.
source: Importantly, however, we observed a parallel persistence of this crosslink pattern with seeding activity (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by XL-MS data shown in Figure 7B,C.

claim: Tau from control brain purified in the monomer fraction.
source: Tau from control brain purified in the monomer fraction (Figure 8A)
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Tau from AD brain distributed across multiple fractions, corresponding to monomer and larger assemblies.
source: while tau from AD brain distributed across multiple fractions, corresponding to monomer and larger assemblies (Figure 8B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: No seeding activity was observed in any control brain fraction.
source: When we tested each fraction for seeding activity, we observed none in any control brain fraction (Figure 8C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: All AD fractions contained seeding activity, including monomer.
source: However, all AD fractions contained seeding activity, including monomer (Figure 8C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Monomer seeding activity was readily observed in tau KO brain spiked with Ms.
source: We readily observed monomer seeding activity in tau KO brain spiked with Ms, however we observed none in fractions that had been spiked with fibrils (Figure 8D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: No monomer seeding activity was observed in tau KO brain fractions that had been spiked with fibrils.
source: We readily observed monomer seeding activity in tau KO brain spiked with Ms, however we observed none in fractions that had been spiked with fibrils (Figure 8D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: Control-derived monomer was inert, even after incubation at RT.
source: Control monomer was inert, even after incubation at RT (Figure 8E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: AD-derived Ms that was purified, frozen, and re-purified by SEC exhibited seeding activity exclusively in the monomer fraction.
source: AD-derived Ms that was purified, frozen, and re-purified by SEC exhibited seeding activity exclusively in the monomer fraction (Figure 8E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: AD-derived Ms incubated at RT formed seed-competent assemblies of increasing size.
source: By contrast, AD-derived Ms incubated at RT formed seed-competent assemblies of increasing size (Figure 8E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8E.

claim: No evidence of the crosslink that marked Ms was observed in control-derived monomer.
source: In control-derived monomer, we observed no evidence of the crosslink that marked Ms (Figure 8G).
evidence: This claim is supported by XL-MS data shown in Figure 8G.

claim: In each AD-derived Ms sample a discrete set of crosslinks between aa150 and aa259-290 was observed.
source: However, in each AD-derived Ms sample we observed a discrete set of crosslinks between aa150 and aa259-290 (Figure 8H).
evidence: This claim is supported by XL-MS data shown in Figure 8H.

claim: The overall energetics and radii of gyration in the models were comparable for Mi and Ms.
source: The overall energetics and radii of gyration in the models were comparable for Mi and Ms (Figure 9—figure supplement 1), indicating global structural similarity.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational modeling data shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: The Mi structural model predicted masking of VQIINK and VQIVYK sequences in compact 'hairpin' structures.
source: The Mi structural model predicted masking of VQIINK and VQIVYK sequences in compact 'hairpin' structures (Figure 9B)
evidence: This claim is based on computational modeling using XL-MS restraints.

claim: Within Ms the model predicted relative exposure of VQIINK and VQIVYK.
source: By contrast, within Ms the model predicted relative exposure of VQIINK and VQIVYK (Figure 9C).
evidence: This claim is based on computational modeling using XL-MS restraints.

claim: Mi from control patients featured VQIINK/VQIVYK sequences in a less accessible configuration.
source: As for recombinant protein, Mi from control patients also featured VQIINK/VQIVYK sequences in a less accessible configuration (Figure 9D).
evidence: This claim is based on computational modeling using XL-MS restraints from patient samples.

claim: In AD-derived Ms, the model predicted an exposed configuration of VQIINK/VQIVYK.
source: In AD-derived Ms, long-range contacts from aa150 to R2 influenced the model, and predicted an exposed configuration of VQIINK/VQIVYK (Figure 9E).
evidence: This claim is based on computational modeling using XL-MS restraints from patient samples.

claim: Differences between the Mi and Ms primarily localized to the RD in limited proteolysis experiments.
source: Differences between the Mi and Ms primarily localized to the RD (Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by limited proteolysis data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1.

claim: In Mi, an R1R2 fragment was enriched in limited proteolysis.
source: In Mi, an R1R2 fragment was enriched (Figure 10C)
evidence: This claim is supported by limited proteolysis data shown in Figure 10C.

claim: In Ms, only the R2 portion of the R1R2 fragment was enriched in limited proteolysis.
source: while only the R2 portion of that fragment was enriched in Ms (Figure 10D).
evidence: This claim is supported by limited proteolysis data shown in Figure 10D.

claim: Similar patterns to R1R2 were observed in R2R3 in limited proteolysis.
source: We observed similar patterns in R2R3 (Figure 10F,G).
evidence: This claim is supported by limited proteolysis data shown in Figure 10F,G.

claim: Proteolysis in Mi preferentially occurred outside the hairpin that includes VQIINK and VQIVYK amyloid sequences.
source: Mapping these cleavage sites onto our structural models revealed that proteolysis in Mi preferentially occurred outside the hairpin that includes VQIINK and VQIVYK amyloid sequences, while cleavage in Ms occurred adjacent to the amyloid sequences (Figure 10I,J).
evidence: This claim is based on mapping proteolysis data onto structural models.

claim: Cleavage in Ms occurred adjacent to the VQIINK and VQIVYK amyloid sequences.
source: Mapping these cleavage sites onto our structural models revealed that proteolysis in Mi preferentially occurred outside the hairpin that includes VQIINK and VQIVYK amyloid sequences, while cleavage in Ms occurred adjacent to the amyloid sequences (Figure 10I,J).
evidence: This claim is based on mapping proteolysis data onto structural models.

claim: Tau monomer occupies two distinct and stable conformational ensembles.
source: We propose that tau monomer occupies two distinct and stable conformational ensembles.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: One set of structures (collectively termed Mi) is relatively inert.
source: One set of structures (collectively termed Mi) is relatively inert
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Another set of structures (collectively termed Ms) has intrinsic ability to self-assemble and acts as a template for fibril growth in vitro and in cells.
source: while another has intrinsic ability to self-assemble, and acts as a template, or seed, for fibril growth in vitro and in cells (collectively termed Ms).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Tau monomer purified from AD brain had intrinsic seeding activity.
source: Tau monomer purified from AD brain also had intrinsic seeding activity, and self-associated to produce larger seed-competent assemblies.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Tau monomer purified from AD brain self-associated to produce larger seed-competent assemblies.
source: Tau monomer purified from AD brain also had intrinsic seeding activity, and self-associated to produce larger seed-competent assemblies.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: VQIVYK and VQIINK sequences assume an open configuration in all types of Ms (fibril-derived, heparin-induced, and AD-derived).
source: A model restrained by the XL-MS data, and consistent with biochemical studies, predicts that VQIVYK and VQIINK sequences assume an open configuration in all types of Ms (fibril-derived, heparin-induced, and AD-derived).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from computational modeling and biochemical data.

claim: The model predicts lack of VQIINK/VQIVYK exposure in Mi.
source: By contrast, the model predicts lack of VQIINK/VQIVYK exposure in Mi.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from computational modeling.

claim: Limited proteolysis studies are consistent with the idea of differential exposure of VQIINK/VQIVYK sequences in Mi vs. Ms.
source: Limited proteolysis studies are consistent with this idea
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from limited proteolysis data.

claim: Mandelkow et al. have previously proposed native tau structure to be in a 'paperclip' configuration, with the C-terminus folded over the RD based on intramolecular FRET and electron paramagnetic resonance spin labeling.
source: Based on intramolecular FRET and electron paramagnetic resonance spin labeling Mandelkow et al. have previously proposed native tau structure to be in a 'paperclip' configuration, with the C-terminus folded over the RD (Jeganathan et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: The structure of microtubule-bound tau previously determined by NMR is similar to the Mi structural model with VQIINK and VQIVYK sequences in compact 'hairpin' structures.
source: The Mi structural model predicted masking of VQIINK and VQIVYK sequences in compact 'hairpin' structures (Figure 9B), similar to the structure of microtubule-bound tau previously determined by NMR (Kadavath et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work and comparison with the current modeling data.

claim: In AD-derived tau fibrils the VQIVYK sequence plays a key role in the core amyloid structure (along with adjacent amino acids), but the VQIINK sequence does not.
source: Consistent with this idea, the Fitzpatrick et al. study indicates that in AD-derived tau fibrils the VQIVYK sequence plays a key role in the core amyloid structure (along with adjacent amino acids), but the VQIINK sequence does not (Fitzpatrick et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Heparin binding involves residues spanning 270–290, and promotes expansion of the remainder of the molecule.
source: Indeed, it has been recently observed that heparin binding involves residues spanning 270–290, and promotes expansion of the remainder of the molecule (Zhao et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Multiple disease-associated mutations in tau affect residues in close proximity to VQIINK/VQIVYK.
source: We also note that multiple disease-associated mutations in tau affect residues in close proximity to VQIINK/VQIVYK.
evidence: This is a statement based on knowledge of disease-associated mutations.

claim: Serine or leucine substitutions at P301 would uniquely destabilize the local structure and promote exposure of the VQIINK/VQIVYK sequences according to the models.
source: For example, our models predict that serine or leucine substitutions at P301 (which cause dominantly inherited tauopathy) would uniquely destabilize the local structure and promote exposure of the VQIINK/VQIVYK sequences.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the computational models.
